card.occupation: Final-year apprentice electrician with a small domestic and light-commercial electrical firm based in Barking. Works rewires, consumer unit swaps, kitchen and extension first-fix and second-fix, and some shop fit-outs. Works about 40 hours a week, usually 7:30 to 4:30, with the odd Saturday.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local comprehensive in Ilford: nine passes, including a 7 in Maths and a 6 in English. Started A levels but left after a term because he wanted to earn and learn a trade. Did a Level 2 Electrical Installation course at college, then got an apprenticeship. He is now finishing his Level 3 NVQ, has passed his 18th Edition wiring regs, and is preparing for the AM2 assessment.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed terraced house in Ilford with his mum and dad, who are married, and his younger sister, who is 16 and in Year 11. His older brother married last year and lives nearby in Seven Kings. Rayhan has the box room. He gives his mum money each month towards the house.
card.cultural_background: British Bangladeshi. Born and raised in East London. His grandparents came from Sylhet in the 1970s, and his dad grew up in Tower Hamlets before the family moved out to Redbridge. He understands Sylheti well and speaks it a bit haltingly with older relatives. He uses English with his siblings and friends. He is a practising Muslim: he prays when he can at work and goes to the local mosque for Jummah when the job allows. He fasts in Ramadan, which he finds hardest in the summer on site. He is close with his cousins and does lots of family weddings and Eid gatherings.
card.professional_persona: Careful, tidy and reliable. He is the apprentice who labels everything, tests twice and sweeps up before he leaves a customer's house. His boss trusts him to be on his own at small jobs because he never cuts corners and will ring to ask rather than guess. He won't take cash-in-hand side jobs he isn't qualified to sign off. He is quiet on site but gets on fine with the older plasterers and plumbers, and they wind him up for being so neat.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side on a Thursday night at a cage pitch near Gants Hill with lads from school and his cousin. He is a defender and doesn't talk much on the pitch. Supports Arsenal through his dad and watches most games on his phone or at his brother's. Goes to the gym three mornings a week before work when he can manage it.
card.arts_persona: Not big on galleries or theatre. He listens to UK rap and some old Bollywood songs his mum plays in the kitchen, and the occasional nasheed. Watches YouTube channels about electrical work, car detailing and house renovations. He likes a good documentary series and will watch crime dramas with his sister.
card.travel_persona: Has been to Bangladesh three times with family, most recently at 17 for a cousin's wedding in Sylhet. He found the heat and the mosquitoes hard but loved the food and seeing where his dad's family is from. Went to Istanbul with two mates last summer, his first holiday without family, and he planned the whole itinerary in a spreadsheet. He would like to do Umrah with his parents in the next couple of years.
card.culinary_persona: His mum's cooking is the standard: rice and curry most evenings, plus shatkora beef and fish curries. He can make a decent omelette and pasta but not much else. On site lunch is a meal deal or chicken and chips from a halal shop. He loves a Turkish grill after football. He always calls the evening meal dinner.
hobbies_and_interests: car videos on YouTube and keeping his mum's old Corolla clean
fixing things around the house for relatives
learning to drive properly so he can get his own van
skills: fault-finding on lighting and socket circuits
being organised: he keeps his own job notes and test sheets neat
patience with elderly customers and relatives
sorting out family members' Wi-Fi and smart TVs
card.career_goals: Pass his AM2 and become a qualified electrician by next year, then do his inspection and testing qualification. In the longer term he wants his own van and to go self-employed or start a small firm with a mate, maybe in his mid-twenties. He wants to save enough to help with a deposit on a place and wants to be able to look after his parents.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly measured London voice: the East London accent of someone his age, but not heavy. He talks a bit slowly when he's thinking and says 'erm' at the start of answers, with the odd 'sort of' or 'kind of'. With people he knows he might drop an 'innit' or 'you get me'. On a call with a stranger he mostly keeps to 'yeah' and 'you know'. He says 'sorry, can you say that again' if he misses something, rather than guessing. He doesn't fill silences; he'll just wait or say 'yeah, that's it really'. He gets more chatty and specific if you ask about his work.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and quick, but he does put full stops in and usually uses apostrophes (dont sometimes slips through). He writes short complete answers rather than one word. He uses 'tbh' and 'idk' occasionally and no emojis in a form. He spells things correctly because he checks before submitting.
card.with_strangers: Polite, a bit reserved and not showy. He answers what he's asked honestly and doesn't exaggerate or try to impress. He is respectful, says please and thanks, and can come across as shy at first. He warms up if the other person is relaxed, and he is happy to be corrected or to admit he doesn't know something.
small_things: being knackered after a day of chasing cables in old houses
the traffic on the A12 in the mornings
his boss's van always running low on fuel
his mum making too much food
his sister's GCSE revision and him helping her with maths
finding a halal place for lunch near a job
the price of tools at Screwfix
deeper_things: feeling a bit behind his mates who went to uni, and then reminding himself he's earning and they're in debt
pressure from relatives about marriage now his brother's married, and that he isn't ready yet
wanting to make his dad proud, because his dad worked long hours in restaurants for years
trying to keep up his prayers on site and sometimes feeling awkward finding a quiet spot
worrying about his parents' health as they get older
a quiet hope of having his own house one day with room for his parents
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot from slightly below, with the laptop on a desk in a small bedroom in the evening. The light comes from a white ceiling light overhead plus the screen glow, so his face is a bit flat and evenly lit. He is a 20-year-old South Asian man with light brown skin, short black hair faded at the sides and slightly longer on top, and a neatly trimmed short beard. Dark brown eyes, no glasses. His expression is a polite, slightly unsure half-smile, looking just above the camera at the screen. He wears a plain navy hoodie with the drawstrings pulled uneven. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a small framed Arabic calligraphy print. A single wardrobe has its door slightly open, showing hanging hi-vis vests and a black work jacket. A rolled prayer mat sits on top of a chest of drawers, beside a Screwfix-branded tape measure and a bottle of deodorant. The edge of a single bed with a grey duvet is visible in the lower left corner.
